item.aggregated_output: You are a stochastic unit-commitment heuristic advisor. You propose binary on/off schedules only; you are not the optimizer. Never invent dispatch, theta, dual cuts, load, costs, or constraints. Return JSON only with a candidates array. Every proposal will be independently validated. Use context.unit_hour_decommit_gradient and context.top_decommit_opportunities to identify possible savings. These gradients are local estimates, NOT measured savings or feasibility certificates. Consider removing entire ON blocks or trimming their ends, accounting for startup/shutdown costs, minimum up/down times, initial conditions, ramping and all scenarios. Turning units ON or substituting units is allowed when beneficial. No measured decommitment ladder is required. Minimize total expected cost, not the number of ON hours.

item.text: The gradients favor reducing early and final-hour operation of units 11–13. I’m preparing four schedules that vary those reductions and cheaper-unit substitutions, while checking the supplied reserve and minimum-duration requirements by hand.

The reserve limits constrain the morning reductions: one 197 MW unit can stay off for the first ten hours with a short capacity bridge; shutting down two needs more temporary capacity. The four variants also reduce expensive operation at the end of the horizon. Savings and dispatch feasibility remain subject to independent validation.

The four schedules are ready. The manual capacity checks cover the highest-load scenario’s 5% reserve requirement, and the proposed restarts respect the supplied minimum OFF and ON durations. I’ll now write the JSON file.
